short_description: A bacterium whose entire genome was designed on a computer, chemically synthesised, and pared down to the essentials: JCVI-syn3.0 (2016) got by on just 473 genes, roughly half of what its nearest natural relative, Mycoplasma mycoides, carries. The later, division-stable version, JCVI-syn3A (2021), adds a handful back. It was not built from scratch, and roughly a third of its genes still have no known function.
morphology_summary: Wall-less Mollicute derivative: bounded only by a single plasma membrane (no peptidoglycan wall, no outer membrane), roughly spherical/pleomorphic, ~400 nm diameter (near/below the diffraction limit of light). Interior: one circular synthetic chromosome (no nuclear envelope), ribosomes, unstructured cytoplasm; no organelles, no flagella/pili/capsule. JCVI-syn3.0 (473 genes) divides into irregular blobs; JCVI-syn3A (493 genes) divides into regular round daughter cells -- the corrected behaviour the catalogue names.
honesty_points: Not built from scratch: only the genome (a DNA molecule) was chemically synthesised; it was transplanted into an already-living, emptied recipient cell of a related Mycoplasma species (M. capricolum in the actual JCVI lineage), which then ran on the new instructions. Never depict assembly from non-living parts.

Roughly a third (~149 of 473 in syn3.0) of the genes have no known function despite being essential -- textual/label fact, not directly picturable; carried into labels.unknown_gene_products and every descriptions.json block.
